'''Balanos Vasilopoulos''' ({{langx|el|Μπαλάνος Βασιλόπουλος}}; 1694–1760) was a [[Greeks|Greek]] [[Eastern Orthodox|Orthodox]] cleric, author, mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.  He is known for attempting to solve [[doubling the cube]].  He was one of the most influential Greek mathematicians of the 18th century.  His teacher was the notable scientist [[Methodios Anthrakites]].  He made a significant contribution to the [[Modern Greek Enlightenment]] during the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] occupation of the Greek world.<ref name="math">{{cite web
|url= https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=el&tl=en&u=http%3A%2F%2Fdlab.phs.uoa.gr%2Findex.php%2Fviographika%2Fdetails%2F6%2F46&sandbox=1
|title=   Balanos Vassilopoulos
|publisher=   Department of History and Philosophy of Science of the University of Athens
|author=   E. Amygdalaki A. Paraskevopoulou
|date=     May 14, 2021
|accessdate= May 14, 2021}}</ref>

==Life==
Balanos was born in [[Ioannina]], a major center of the Greek Enlightenment movement during that time.<ref>[http://pandektis.ekt.gr/pandektis/handle/10442/69082 Balanos Vasilopoulos]. Πανδέκτης, Νεοελληνική Εικονιστική Προσωπογραφία.</ref> He was a student of [[Methodios Anthrakites]] director of the local Gouma (later Balaneios) school. As a teacher, he initially became director of the school Epifaneios Igoumenos (1719–1734) and then the Gouma. Both schools were the most prestigious in Ioannina.

Regarding the [[Greek language question]], he supported the conservative party and teaching classical Greek in education.  [[Eugenios Voulgaris]] accused Balanos of not supporting the progressive [[Demotic Greek|Demotic]].<ref>{{citation |last= Dēmaras|first= Kōnstantinos |title=A history of modern Greek literature |publisher=SUNY Press |year=1972 |page = 136|isbn=978-0-87395-071-8|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=p3GHlQL9mbAC }}</ref> In ca. 1760 his son [[Kosmas Balanos]] succeeded him as schoolmaster of the Gouma School.<ref name=UniAthens>[http://195.134.75.14/hellinomnimon/authors/InfoAuthors/Balanos%20K.htm Μπαλάνος Κοσμάς 1731, Ιωάννινα – 1807/8, Ιωάννινα] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402232512/http://195.134.75.14/hellinomnimon/authors/InfoAuthors/Balanos%20K.htm |date=2012-04-02 }} Ελληνομνήμων. University of Athens database.</ref>

==Work==

Because he experienced the [[Methodios Anthrakites|Methodios Affair]] first hand he was a strict teacher of [[Korydalism]].  On the other hand, he expanded and reprinted the work of his teacher Methodios Anthrakites ''The Way of Mathematics'' ({{langx|el|Οδός Μαθηματική}}, 1749).<ref>{{citation |last= Kostantaras|first= Dean J. |title=Infamy and revolt: the rise of the national problem in early modern Greek thought  |publisher= East European Monographs |year=2006| page = 164|isbn=978-0-88033-581-2|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CNYDAQAAIAAJ&q=Balanos+Vasilopoulos}}</ref> This was the first handbook in the field of mathematics published in Greek during the [[Ottoman Greece|Ottoman occupation]].<ref>{{citation |last= Sakellariou|first= M. V. |title=Epirus, 4000 years of Greek history and civilization|publisher=Ekdotike Athenon |year=1997 |isbn=978-960-213-371-2|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UV1oAAAAMAAJ&q=handbook |page=268 }}</ref> He also wrote the following, and various other books of less significance:

*''Έκθεσις ακριβεστάτη της αριθμητικής (Precise Exposition of Arithmetic)'', Venice, 1803
*''Ερμηνεία εις τους αφορισμούς του Ιπποκράτους (Interpretation of the Aphorisms of [[Hippocrates]])''

Balanos claimed to have solved the problem of [[doubling the cube]], i.e. finding the cube root of 2 using ruler and compasses. He published this in [[Venice]] in 1756, and attempted to gain international recognition for his solution from the community of mathematicians, and in particular [[Leonhard Euler]] and the members of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences|Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences]]. His son [[Kosmas Balanos]] rejected the solution in a work published in 1816 after his own death, ''Αντιπελάργησις'' (''Antipelargisis, Against the Stork''). The problem was later proved to be impossible.<ref name=Christine>{{cite journal|last=Phili|first=Christine|title=Greek mathematical publications in Vienna in the 18th–19th centuries|journal=Mathematics in the Austrian-Hungarian Empire. Proceedings of a Symposium Held in Budapest on August 1, 2009 During the XXIII ICHST.|pages=137–148|url=http://dml.cz/bitstream/handle/10338.dmlcz/400826/DejinyMat_41-2010-1_18.pdf}}</ref><ref>Lambrou, Michael. “An attempt to duplicate the cube during Ottoman times, and the text of ‘Antipelargisis’”. (Euclides, 11 (1994) 41-67). Cited in his [http://www.uninettunointernational.net/e/COCode/06Teachers/CUCurricprof/01curriculum.asp?id=0203CO06CU01000002000000000300010900&profid=2480&courseid=3565&langid=1&degreeid=140&planid=109&newlanguage=2 Curriculum Vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120326024440/http://www.uninettunointernational.net/e/COCode/06Teachers/CUCurricprof/01curriculum.asp?id=0203CO06CU01000002000000000300010900&profid=2480&courseid=3565&langid=1&degreeid=140&planid=109&newlanguage=2 |date=2012-03-26 }}, retrieved 25 June 2011.</ref>
